newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco deal possible this week - sources.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco deal possible this week - sources.

text.p: Attorneys general are optimistic they can present the White House with a tobacco settlement proposal this week, although some problem areas such as punitive damages may be unresolved, sources close to the talks said Monday.

Two key negotiators, Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore and plaintiffs lawyer Dick Scruggs, met with White House staff early Monday afternoon to provide an update on progress. The two men met with tobacco industry representatives earlier Monday.
Sources said some negotiators hope to have a proposal to the White House as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday.
Moore would not comment on when a proposal might be finished. However, he told Reuters "things are going real well. We're gonna get there."
A large group of attorneys general were involved in a meeting Monday afternoon to discuss various issues, including language in a settlement that would make it binding in each of their states.
A news briefing was set for later Monday.

The attorneys general, the highest ranking legal officers of each state, and the tobacco industry have been negotiating since early April. Mississippi's Moore has been trying to reach a deal prior to his state's Medicaid trial against the industry, set to begin July 7.
The attorneys general are suing the tobacco industry to recoup the costs of treating diseases allegedly caused by smoking.
